title: PowerPoint on desktop: Copilot Agent Mode applies an attached deck's theme and styles to a new presentation
notes: claim 58: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
the verifier wrote "hold" but listed no blocker and fewer than three majors; the claims decide, so the page is not held
summary: The roadmap details, licence-assignment control and documented attachment steps check out. However, Microsoft does not state that nothing changes for everyone who does not attach a deck, and the briefing also overstates how the user's file choice bounds Copilot's data access.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: Using the attached-deck styling capability is a user choice, classified as user-opt-in.
claims.quote:
Use the 'Attach file' feature to select an existing PowerPoint deck.
Request Copilot to generate slides using the attached deck's style.

claims.claim: Feature-specific admin prerequisites for attaching a deck are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode attached deck style admin enable disable prerequisites Anthropic; PowerPoint Agent Mode admin policy attached files disable Graph PowerShell. Opened release-notes and wordexcelppt-agents; the latter describes agents within the Microsoft Copilot app, not this attachment.

claims.claim: The pages read do not say existing behaviour changes for users who do not attach a deck.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot in PowerPoint attached deck style default unchanged users who do not attach. Opened release-notes and read the attached-deck entry; it gives attachment steps, not behaviour for users who omit them.

claims.claim: The feature reads the deck the user attaches.
claims.quote: you can reference an existing PowerPoint file, so Copilot applies its theme and styles to the new deck

claims.claim: What Copilot can see is set by the user's choice of attached file.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint attached deck style uses slide content only theme; attached presentation style theme permissions. Opened release-notes and copilot-overview. The feature entry identifies a styling input but does not define the full boundary of data Copilot can see.
claims.fix: Remove 'so what Copilot can see is set by that user's choice of file'. Keep 'The feature reads a deck the user attaches' and the existing statement that the release notes do not describe whether slide content is used.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The release-notes entry for this feature does not say whether the attached deck's slide content is also used.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint attached deck style uses slide content only theme. Opened release-notes: the 555878/555880 entry describes theme and styles, not slide content. Its separate July entry about content reuse names different roadmap IDs, 555887, 555889 and 555892.

claims.claim: The release notes and roadmap describe no new sign-in for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint attached presentation style theme sign-in connector permissions automatic without prompt admin settings. Read the roadmap description and the complete feature entry in release-notes; neither describes a new sign-in.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published which licence tier covers this attached-deck feature specifically.

Opened release-notes, copilot-overview, copilot-license-options and wordexcelppt-agents. No feature-tier statement found; the agents page's paid requirement is for agents within Microsoft Copilot.

claims.claim: No credit rate specific to attaching a deck's style is published at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint reference attached presentation style theme credit rate meter; Copilot PowerPoint credits billing. Opened release-notes, copilot-overview, usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits and usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits; no attached-deck rate found.

claims.claim: No separate meter specific to this attached-deck styling feature is published.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint reference attached presentation style theme credit rate meter; Copilot PowerPoint credits billing. Opened usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits and copilot-overview; models with usage-based billing are listed, but no meter specific to this attachment is identified.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Low is the known incremental cost rating: admin time and communication, while feature-specific licence and meter details remain unpublished.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint attached deck style licensing Basic credit rate meter; Copilot PowerPoint credits billing. Read release-notes, copilot-overview and usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits. No incremental licence or feature-specific meter found; SCHEMA permits low for known indirect costs.

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least the License Administrator or User Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. ... Select the row of the user ... select Licenses and Apps. ... Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.where: controls[0].governs; controls[0].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: User licence assignment governs entitlement to the licensed Copilot in PowerPoint experience as a whole.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: The documented licence-assignment operation is not an attachment-specific switch.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: An admin setting specifically governing Agent Mode or deck attachment in PowerPoint remains unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode admin policy attached files disable Graph PowerShell; PowerPoint Agent Mode disable. Opened release-notes, copilot-overview and wordexcelppt-agents. The latter documents a Copilot-app agents control, not a PowerPoint attachment setting.

claims.claim: Learn describes an Anthropic-model enablement requirement for Word, Excel and PowerPoint Agents in the Microsoft Copilot app.
claims.quote: These agents exclusively use Anthropic's AI models. This AI model must be enabled. These requirements are mandatory for Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Agents to function.

claims.claim: Whether Agent Mode in PowerPoint depends on the Copilot-app agents' Anthropic setting remains unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode attached deck style admin enable disable prerequisites Anthropic; PowerPoint Agent Mode licensing admin. Read wordexcelppt-agents and release-notes: the agents page places its agents within Microsoft Copilot, without identifying this in-PowerPoint attachment capability.

claims.claim: Only desktop Copilot users who choose to attach a deck will notice this change, and nothing changes for anyone else.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot in PowerPoint attached deck style default unchanged users who do not attach. Read the roadmap and the complete 555878/555880 release-notes entry. They describe selecting and using a deck; neither states that all other users' behaviour remains unchanged.
claims.fix: Replace the impact rationale with: 'Low. The documented workflow is a user-selected attachment in Copilot in PowerPoint on desktop; no source reviewed says existing behaviour changes for users who do not attach a deck.' Keep the user-opt-in default and the low impact rating.
